_what_this_is: The entry gate, answered BEFORE drafting. The threshold question is whether a well-informed non-expert would confidently believe something the primary sources do not support.

belief._note: What the reader already believes, stated as they would state it. If you cannot write this sentence, there is nothing to correct and no subject -- which is how the tobacco-analogy candidate died.
belief.statement: Removing CO2 from the air, mostly by planting trees and eventually with direct air capture machines, is a useful backup. But it is expensive, unproven at scale and risks being used as an excuse to keep burning fossil fuels. Cutting emissions is what really matters, and removal can only mop up a small remainder later.
belief.how_we_know_they_believe_it: The coverage that settled it. Named outlets, quoted headlines. Not 'it is widely assumed'.

carried_by.by: a model's reading (claude-sonnet-4-6, web search), verified by code: the page was fetched with the honest client and contains the belief's key words

what_the_sources_show.statement: The sources say rapid emissions cuts are the dominant source of mitigation potential in the coming decades, but CDR 'will also have an important role to play'. Even low estimates imply several gigatons of removals by mid-century, and national CDR proposals fall short of 1.5 °C scenarios.
what_the_sources_show.by: a model's reading (claude-opus-5-5, from held sources), the quotation verified verbatim by code

direction._note: CORRECTS, CONFIRMS or NARROWS. This field exists so the contrarianism guard can count. A publication whose answer is always CORRECTS is performing scepticism rather than assessing evidence, and is not to be trusted.
direction.by: a model's reading (claude-opus-5-5, from held sources), the quotation verified verbatim by code
direction.why: The sources back the belief that emissions cuts come first and that deployment is lagging, but they contradict the idea that removal only mops up a small remainder later, since even low estimates require several gigatons by mid-century, against about 2 GtCO2 per year today, mostly from conventional

reader_with_a_decision: A policymaker or corporate sustainability lead deciding how much to rely on, fund or buy carbon removal alongside direct emission cuts in a net-zero plan, and on what timeline.

public_record_check._note: NOT 'has anybody published this'. On any contested question, somebody has. The question is whether it has been carried WHERE THIS READER WOULD FIND IT. Run the counterexample hunter on the belief statement, not on the finding.
public_record_check.carried_in_general_coverage: Yes: New Republic (https://newrepublic.com/article/215140/carbon-capture-wont-save-us-anytime-soon), fetched 2026-11-27, sha256 33a81e591d936143; the page contains 19 of the belief's 29 key words. A model's reading (web search), checked by code.
public_record_check.our_contribution: translation, extension, or correction of the prior art -- say which

kill_condition: Primary sources (IPCC AR6 mitigation pathways, national net-zero plans, measured removal inventories) would have to show two things. First, that pathways reaching net zero need little or no CO2 removal beyond what existing forests and land already provide. Second, that current removal capacity, including novel methods, is already on track to meet whatever amount is needed. Then removal's role would be the minor, already-understood footnote people assume, and there would be no story.

kill_condition_tested.by: a model's reading (claude-opus-5-5, from held sources), the quotation verified verbatim by code
kill_condition_tested.note: The sources show the opposite of both kill conditions: pathways need several gigatons of removals, no country yet commits to substantively scaling novel methods, and deployment is behind expectations and short of what pathways need.

scope._note: What the answer will and will not cover, written at step 1 BEFORE any source is opened, so scope cannot be fitted to the findings afterwards. An omission ruled OUT_OF_SCOPE, and a headline conclusion declared out of scope, must name the question's words or one of these entries (fix 2, docs/whu-fix2-omission-rulings-design.md section 2.4).
scope.covers: The role of carbon dioxide removal (land-based methods such as afforestation and soil carbon, and engineered methods such as direct air capture with storage, BECCS, enhanced weathering and biochar) in reaching net-zero CO2 and GHG emissions. It covers how much removal net-zero pathways require and when, what it is needed for (counterbalancing hard-to-abate residual emissions, and achieving net-negative emissions later), how much removal happens today, and the constraints on scaling it: cost, land, energy, storage durability and verification.

out.what: Solar radiation management and other non-CO2 geoengineering
out.why: These do not remove carbon. They are a different intervention with different evidence and risks.

out.what: Carbon capture and storage on fossil-fuel power plants or industrial point sources
out.why: This reduces new emissions rather than removing CO2 already in the air, so it belongs to the emissions-cutting side of the question.

out.what: Integrity and quality of specific voluntary carbon offset credits or companies' net-zero claims
out.why: This is a market and accountability question that needs its own case-by-case evidence. It is distinct from removal's physical role.

out.what: Which particular removal technology or company is the best investment
out.why: The page assesses removal's overall role, not comparative commercial prospects.

out.what: Non-CO2 greenhouse gases such as methane, and their removal
out.why: The question concerns carbon dioxide removal specifically.

evidence_standard._note: What kinds of evidence the answer will weigh, written at step 1 BEFORE any source is opened (post-study fix 3, docs/whu-fix3-evidence-standard.md). 'measured': outcomes measured in trials, cohorts, evaluations. 'assessed': expert assessments -- systematic-review conclusions, IPCC confidence-rated statements, guideline recommendations. When they differ, the page states both and drops neither.
evidence_standard.measured: Quantities that are observed or reported: current annual CO2 removal, split into conventional land-based and novel methods (in tonnes or gigatonnes per year). Deployed and announced capacity of direct air capture and BECCS facilities. Observed costs per tonne. Measured storage permanence and reversal rates. Cumulative and annual removal volumes required in modelled net-zero pathways, taken from published scenario databases.
evidence_standard.assessed: Expert-panel or review judgements carrying confidence or likelihood ratings. Examples are IPCC AR6 statements that CDR is unavoidable for net zero to counterbalance residual emissions, with the stated confidence level. Assessments of the feasibility, sustainability limits, and co-benefits and risks of scaling each removal method. Judgements in syntheses such as the State of Carbon Dioxide Removal report on the gap between planned and required removal.
